core.title: Commons application modules do not import integration
core.given: A module of the application role in the shared (commons) code tree — orchestration over ports it defines
core.when: it adds or keeps an import that resolves into the integration layer of that shared tree
core.then: The module MUST NOT import from the integration layer of the shared code tree.
prefer: Canonical path: keep application code in the shared tree dependent on an application-facing port.
Canonical path: let integration implement that port and the composition root supply it.
During GREEN: first reuse an existing port that already represents the required capability.
During GREEN: add the smallest missing port only when current behavior genuinely needs an outer capability.
During GREEN: pass only the data or collaborator required by the acceptance.
avoid: Importing integration directly as a shortcut to GREEN.
Introducing a generalized service layer for future callers.
Reorganizing unrelated modules in the shared tree.
unless: Test files and the profile's never-scanned (vendored/build) trees are not scanned by this rule.
Imports of external packages resolve outside the project graph and are not layer-checked.
A file with no layer-role assignment is outside these rules, not in violation.
core.why: Application orchestrates through ports it defines; reaching into integration inverts the dependency and welds orchestration to a transport, so changing the transport changes the orchestration.
evidence: The shared-tree application layer has no integration dependency: the stack's architecture check reports no import from an application-role module in the shared tree resolving into the integration layer.
verification: Flag an import from an application-role module in the shared (commons) code tree that resolves into the integration layer, whether newly added or already present.
Skip test files and the profile's never-scanned vendored/build trees entirely; the exact exclusion classification is owned by the stack's checker.
Do not layer-check imports of external packages; they resolve outside the project graph.
Files with no layer-role assignment are out of scope, not violations.

fires: An application-role module in the shared code tree has a project-internal import (added or pre-existing) that resolves into the integration layer.
An application module in the shared tree imports a transport client or adapter from the integration layer to make an acceptance pass quickly.
doesNotFire: A test file located in the shared application tree imports from integration (test files are never scanned).
A file in a never-scanned vendored or build tree imports from integration.
An application module in the shared tree imports an external package specifier (resolved outside the project graph).
A file with no layer-role assignment imports from integration.
An application module in the shared tree imports an application-facing port it defines.

neutralityNotes: The core keeps 'commons/shared code tree' as a structural concept whose concrete location comes entirely from the profile (layout.commons_dir, roles.application.path, roles.integration.path), so no path appears in the core. The Bun import idioms ('bare npm specifier' for external packages, 'relative or project-alias import' for project-internal ones) are carried by idiom.external_import. Detector and finding ids (bun_clean_architecture_detector and its finding id) have no neutral equivalent and stay in the realization. Severity 3 and strict disposition are per-rule facts kept in core verification. The never-scanned vendored/build trees are the stack-wide roots.excluded list from the profile; the exact exclusion classification is deferred to the stack's checker in core verification. The import-resolution observer this rule needs is needs_new_observer in every stack.
